sources.name: Crop rotations synergize yield, nutrition, and revenue: a meta-analysis
sources.intendedUse: Multi-continent evidence context and documented variation in crop-rotation outcomes; never a field-level prediction
sources.limitations: Synthesis of heterogeneous field trials, not a prescription for an individual farm. Benefits vary with crop sequence and region; some transitions have adverse tradeoffs. Gross revenue is not profit because input costs were not available consistently.

sources.name: Species diversification in conservation agriculture
sources.owner: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.intendedUse: General mechanisms and objectives to investigate when designing locally relevant rotations
sources.limitations: Broad guidance does not quantify field outcomes or validate a particular crop sequence for any location.

sources.name: Diversifying crop rotation increases food production, reduces net greenhouse gas emissions and improves soil health
sources.intendedUse: North China Plain example of measuring diversified rotation tradeoffs
sources.limitations: Six-year experiment in one regional production system; reported effects and extrapolations are not predictions for other farms.

sources.name: Enhancing Crop-Livestock Systems in Conservation Agriculture: Burkina Faso
sources.owner: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.intendedUse: Example of participatory, local testing of crop diversification in five south-western Burkina Faso communities
sources.limitations: 2010 case report; not a controlled global effect estimate or a transferable field prescription.

sources.name: GBIF Species API and Catalogue of Life eXtended Release
sources.intendedUse: Live worldwide plant-name and family lookup in the Crops discovery view, separate from agronomic evidence
sources.limitations: Taxonomic matches can include plants that are not crops. Species identity and family do not establish local suitability, growing requirements, or rotation benefits. Service requires internet access.

sources.name: FAO Ecocrop crop library
sources.owner: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.intendedUse: External route to a broader worldwide crop reference; no Ecocrop traits are imported into FieldShift recommendations
sources.limitations: FAO says the original catalog was discontinued around 2015. Its broad environmental descriptors need current, locally relevant confirmation.

sources.name: NASA POWER Daily API
sources.intendedUse: Daily regional climate context for a requested point
sources.limitations: Gridded values are not a field weather station; local conditions may differ.

sources.name: Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO)
sources.intendedUse: Mapped soil context for a U.S. pilot
sources.limitations: Map units may contain multiple components and are not exact field laboratory samples.

sources.name: Soil Data Access web service and spatial SQL functions
sources.intendedUse: Lookup map units and their possible components at a pilot coordinate
sources.limitations: Point-to-map-unit intersection gives a mapped polygon; it is not a field sampling result.

sources.name: GPM IMERG V07 half-hourly precipitation image service
sources.intendedUse: Attempted satellite precipitation cross-check, separate from NASA POWER history; daily total withheld unless all 48 UTC slots are valid
sources.limitations: 0.1-degree gridded half-hourly rates are not a field gauge or future water supply. The exact run is unverified. Live metadata checked 2026-10-03 ended at 2025-09-30; tested Iowa days returned only 47 valid in-day slots. Recheck temporal availability, units, and completeness before relying on this service.

sources.name: IMERG product overview and run guidance
sources.intendedUse: Interpret IMERG as a half-hourly precipitation estimate and distinguish Early, Late, and Final runs
sources.limitations: Overview describes the product family; the app must inspect the exact service layer and returned units before treating a sample as daily accumulation.

sources.name: 2025 Iowa State Agriculture Overview
sources.intendedUse: Identify major Iowa crops; state figures are not county or field suitability
sources.limitations: State aggregate, not specific to central Iowa

sources.name: 2024 Iowa Crop Progress Review
sources.intendedUse: Broad Iowa planting and harvest season context
sources.limitations: One-year state report, not a date prescription

sources.name: Cover Crop Resources
sources.intendedUse: Iowa corn-soy cover-crop patterns
sources.limitations: Beginner recipes need adaptation to local management

sources.name: Most Commonly Used Cover Crops in Iowa
sources.intendedUse: Cover crop types, overwintering, and management tradeoffs
sources.limitations: General Iowa guidance, not field-specific performance

sources.name: Types of Cover Crops for Use in Home Vegetable Gardens
sources.intendedUse: Species identity and qualitative cover-crop traits only
sources.limitations: Home vegetable gardens are a different management system from commercial row crops; do not transfer ratings directly into recommendation scores

sources.name: Iowa Cover Crop Recipe: Post Corn, Going to Soybean
sources.owner: Iowa State University Extension and Midwest Cover Crops Council
sources.intendedUse: Central Iowa cereal rye timing and corn-to-soybean cover window
sources.limitations: Introductory recipe, not an exact planting date for every field

sources.name: Terminating cover crops ahead of corn
sources.intendedUse: Potential corn establishment and disease risks after winter cereal rye
sources.limitations: Risk depends on termination, weather, and management

sources.name: Influence of Drought on Corn and Soybean
sources.intendedUse: Qualitative crop-stage water sensitivity
sources.limitations: Does not provide field water needs from annual rainfall alone

sources.name: Soil-test interpretations for liming decisions
sources.intendedUse: Conditional Iowa pH targets for corn, soybean, and alfalfa
sources.limitations: Corn/soy target depends on subsoil; not a universal pH range

sources.name: Floods
sources.intendedUse: Regional flood and erosion context
sources.limitations: Hazard description does not establish individual field risk

sources.name: July 2025 Weather Update
sources.intendedUse: Example of rainfall and dryness variability
sources.limitations: One period is not a long-term climate trend

sources.name: Adding alfalfa benefits corn-soybean rotations
sources.intendedUse: Upper Midwest diversified rotation pattern and potential benefits
sources.limitations: Minnesota trial and management systems may not transfer directly to a central Iowa field

sources.name: Value of crop rotation in nitrogen management
sources.intendedUse: Qualitative Iowa rotation and nitrogen context
sources.limitations: Does not establish a crop-specific field nitrogen credit

sources.name: Understanding rye cover crop effects on corn
sources.intendedUse: Rye biomass and water/nitrogen management tradeoffs
sources.limitations: Research synthesis cannot predict field-specific outcome

sources.name: USDA ARS Cover Crop Chart, version 4.0
sources.intendedUse: Qualitative crop type and relative water use
sources.limitations: Broad species-level chart, not local water requirement or field outcome

sources.name: Oilseed radish Plant Guide
sources.intendedUse: Radish growing period and taproot context
sources.limitations: Guide draws on multiple regions; local Iowa feasibility still requires review

sources.name: MODIS Vegetation Indices
sources.intendedUse: Potential vegetation-greenness context
sources.limitations: Greenness is not crop identity, yield, or direct soil health.

sources.name: SoilGrids
sources.intendedUse: Potential modeled global soil context after a stable access method is validated
sources.limitations: ISRIC currently says its beta REST API is paused. WCS and WebDAV are alternatives but have not been integrated or validated here. Modeled estimates include spatial and prediction uncertainty.

sources.name: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6
sources.intendedUse: Potential long-term climate-scenario comparison
sources.limitations: Climate scenarios are not next-season weather forecasts.

sources.name: Persistence of Cover Crop Use in Crop Production in the United States, 2012–2022
sources.intendedUse: National context that cover-crop adoption and persistence vary; not a field-level success prediction
sources.limitations: U.S. multi-source historical analysis; the overview does not provide a central-Iowa field estimate or explain the reason for any individual farm discontinuing use.

sources.name: Economics of Cover Crops
sources.owner: Iowa State University Extension Ag Decision Maker
sources.intendedUse: Identify the farm-specific projected and actual cost/benefit scenarios needed before an economic claim
sources.limitations: Worksheets require local numbers; the page does not prove a particular field's net return or supply an app-ready price model.

sources.name: Small grain crop rotations
sources.owner: Wiersma and Ransom, University of Minnesota / NDSU
sources.limitations: Minnesota and North Dakota systems; regional guidance reviewed in 2018, not approval of FieldShift.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped comparison evidence and observation provenance

sources.name: Dual Use of Cover Crops for Forage Production and Soil Health in Dryland Crop Production
sources.owner: Obour, Holman, Simon and Johnson, Kansas State University (2020)
sources.limitations: HB Ranch near Brownell, Kansas, 2015–2019. Site and year effects limit transfer.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped comparison evidence and observation provenance

sources.name: Crop yield and soil condition under ridge and chisel-plow tillage in the northern Corn Belt, USA
sources.owner: Pikul et al., Soil & Tillage Research 60 (2001), 21–33
sources.limitations: Brookings Barnes clay loam; tillage comparison within corn–soybean, not a rotation effect or temporal SOM change.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped comparison evidence and observation provenance

sources.name: Legume-based rotation enhance long-term soil carbon storage in eastern Oregon dryland wheat systems
sources.owner: Ramírez, Calderón, Singh and Machado, Scientific Reports 15, 13842 (2025)
sources.limitations: Archived samples reconstructed by MIR/PLS, unequal sampling years and some estimated bulk densities. Abstract differs from Results/Table 2 rates.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped comparison evidence and observation provenance

sources.name: Green pea nutrient management for the Inland Northwest, east of the Cascades
sources.limitations: Green-pea guidance; cultivar, pathogen and soil differences prevent automatic transfer to every pulse crop.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped comparison evidence and observation provenance

sources.name: SMAP Enhanced L3 Radiometer Global and Polar Grid Daily 9 km Soil Moisture V6
sources.owner: NASA NSIDC DAAC / O’Neill et al. (2023)

sources.name: Global Agro-Ecological Zones v5
sources.limitations: Approximately 1 km key outputs; suitability depends on crop, water regime, input level and period. No point lookup integrated.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped context and pipeline provenance; not automatic suitability.

sources.name: Köppen–Geiger climate maps, version 2
sources.limitations: 1 km climate classification is not field crop suitability. No raster lookup integrated.
sources.intendedUse: Scoped context and pipeline provenance; not automatic suitability.

sources.name: Harmonized World Soil Database v2
sources.limitations: Approximately 1 km mapped inventory, not a laboratory result. No raster lookup integrated.

sources.name: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map
sources.limitations: Average annual extreme minimum temperature; not a worldwide crop rotation or season-length model.
